study type: Retrospective cohort study with network analysis
exposure: COVID-19 pandemic (comparing pre-pandemic 2018-2019 to post-pandemic 2021-2022 periods)
cohort: The study included women in Alabama who gave birth during pre-pandemic (2018-2019) and post-pandemic (2021-2022) periods.
finding: The COVID-19 pandemic was associated with significant adverse changes in maternal health metrics, increased complexity of multimorbidity interactions, and exacerbated ethnicity-based health disparities among women in Alabama.
mod_finding: American Indian or Alaska Native and Black mothers showed substantial increases in previous cesarean rates in the post-pandemic period.
gest_age: Included as a factor for defining premature births
